The Masters Tournament is played annually at Augusta National Golf Club in Augusta, Georgia, USA. As one of the four major championships in men's professional golf, it is the only major held at the same venue every year, typically in early April. Key Details About the Venue: Location: Augusta, Georgia, United States. Course: Augusta National Golf Club, a private course designed by Bobby Jones and Alister MacKenzie. Tradition: The tournament has been held at this location annually since its inception in 1934. Features: Famous for its immaculate conditions, blooming azaleas, and challenging holes known as "Amen Corner" (holes 11, 12, and 13). Unlike other major tournaments that rotate locations, the Masters has always been played at Augusta National.
